name: Artxanda – Iron Belt trenches & memorial
story: Mount Artxanda, above Bilbao, was the last defended position before the city fell. After the Nationalists broke through the Iron Belt (Cinturón de Hierro) at Gaztelumendi on 12 June 1937, Basque and Republican units fell back to Artxanda, where there was a final, bitter defence while civilians were evacuated westwards. The Basque Army withdrew on 18 June and Nationalist troops entered Bilbao on 19 June. Today the summit is a park with a viewpoint over the city. A stretch of restored trench recalls the fighting, and a large 'fingerprint' sculpture (Huella Dactilar) by Juan José Novella honours all those who died in the war.
see: A restored trench section near the Artxanda viewpoint, the fingerprint memorial and a panoramic view over Bilbao.
plan: Take the Artxanda funicular from central Bilbao (about 3 min) or drive up; free, open access. Allow an hour to walk between the viewpoint and the memorial.
